svg.title: DynamicArchitectViewer: DSL parsing, auto layout, live preview, HTML and SVG export
svg.desc: 1. Editing a .dav file and running language diagnostics 2. Computing the layout and reducing edge crossings 3. Resolving the step scene and rendering the live preview 4. Playing step animations and syncing the cursor 5. Exporting a standalone HTML file 6. Re-importing the .dav source from exported HTML 7. Exporting an animated SVG

g.text: The editor notifies the extension host
The extension host passes the .dav source to
The Lezer grammar builds the syntax tree and
symbols are updated in the editor
The validated nodes, groups and edges are passed to
Columns come from longest paths, then
rows are reordered to reduce edge crossings
Deterministic node and group rectangles are passed to
Cumulative state, rail geometry and callouts become a
Player renders the SVG into the preview
webview via DOM APIs without innerHTML
Moving the editor cursor jumps to the matching
step and highlights the active element
Animations run in phase order, with
parallel: true joining the preceding phase
Double-clicking a node looks up its SourceMap
span and posts revealRange to the editor
Writes a self-contained HTML file with escaped #dav-data JSON
The scene of each step is built as the preview builds
it, and the camera is planned by the same rules
Writes one SVG whose animations all last the whole
Editing a .dav file and running language diagnostics
When the .dav file changes in the editor, the extension host parses the syntax tree with Lezer and updates
diagnostics, Quick Fixes, completions and outline symbols.
Computing the layout and reducing edge crossings
computeLayout assigns columns from the longest edge paths, places groups and rows, and runs up to 16
Resolving the step scene and rendering the live preview
resolveView computes cumulative step state, Bezier rails and callout boxes, then buildScene creates the
virtual SVG tree that Player mounts in the webview.
Playing step animations and syncing the cursor
During playback, Player animates packets phase by phase while syncing cursor highlights and double-click
exportHtml embeds the parsed document, layout, used icons and runtime player into a single HTML file
locked down by a SHA-256 Content Security Policy.
Re-importing the .dav source from exported HTML
importContent reads the #dav-data JSON block without executing the HTML page and restores the
exportSvg draws the same scene for every step and moves it with SMIL on one looping clock. The file runs
no script, so it plays as an image in a README on GitHub.
